parts: Lesson 22: Inverse of a Matrix and its Applications — Summary
adj A is the transpose of the matrix of cofactors. For A = [[a, b], [c, d]], adj A = [[d, −b], [−c, a]] (swap the diagonal, change the sign of the off-diagonal). A(adj A) = (adj A)A = |A|I.
A⁻¹ exists only when A is non-singular (|A| ≠ 0): A⁻¹ = (1/|A|) adj A. Then (A⁻¹)⁻¹ = A, (AB)⁻¹ = B⁻¹A⁻¹ and (A')⁻¹ = (A⁻¹)'. For [[k, 2], [3, 4]] to be invertible, 4k − 6 ≠ 0, i.e. k ≠ 3/2.
Write A = IA and apply row operations to both sides until the left side becomes I; then I = (A⁻¹)A. With column operations write A = AI instead. Do not mix row and column operations.
A system AX = B with |A| ≠ 0 has the unique solution X = A⁻¹B. Steps: find |A|, the cofactors, adj A, A⁻¹, then multiply by B.
